title: Establish cohort sensitivity bands and automated mitigation actions for Optimize evaluations
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Define and implement a per-cohort sensitivity framework for Optimize evals that maps observed regression magnitudes to deterministic mitigation actions (traffic shaping, canary pause, auto-rollforward, and human escalation). Deliver a spec, acceptance criteria, and an automated playbook that ties metric deviations to actionable rollbacks and compensations.
problem_statement: Current Optimize evals produce composite regressions across heterogeneous workloads; alerts are noisy and lack graduated remediation. Teams either overreact (full rollback) or underreact (missed customer impact). We need a repeatable mechanism that: 1) detects meaningful regressions per user cohort, 2) classifies severity with bounded false positive rates, and 3) triggers proportionate mitigation automatically or with minimal operator intervention.
goals: Define per-cohort statistical sensitivity bands (green/amber/red) across primary signals (accuracy, safety, latency, cost-per-token)
Specify deterministic mitigation actions mapped to each band (traffic percentage reduction, canary hold, auto-fallback to baseline model, alert routing)
Implement acceptance tests and automated gating so new model variants cannot progress if any cohort enters red without an approved exception
Reduce noisy escalations by 40% in the first quarter after rollout and ensure safe rollouts for high-risk cohorts
non_goals: Designing new evaluation metrics from scratch (we will rely on existing Optimize signals and a small set of derived aggregates)
Changing core runtime routing logic beyond traffic shaping and fallback routing
Replacing manual post-mortem processes for confirmed regressions
success_metrics: % reduction in false-positive rollback alerts (target 40% within 90 days)
Time-to-detect for cohort regressions (median < 5 minutes for streaming signals)
Percentage of rollouts that execute automated mitigation (target 25% of events; remainder require human approval)
Customer-visible degradation incidents due to Optimize changes (target < 1 per quarter for customers with >1M tokens/month)
Precision and recall for regression detection per cohort (precision >= 0.85, recall >= 0.7 for P1/P0 cohorts)
acceptance_criteria: Specification doc approved by Product, Applied ML, Runtime, and Reliability (signoffs captured in Confluence)
Implementation of sensitivity bands for at least three prototype cohorts: Free-tier chat, High-throughput embeddings, Regulated (private) customers
Automated mapping from signal band to mitigation action implemented and feature-flagged in the control plane
End-to-end CI tests that simulate injected regressions produce the expected mitigation (traffic reduction, canary hold, fallback) in a staging environment
Dashboard panels in Console that surface cohort-level band state and the last action taken, with links to the triggering eval run and PRs
Runbook created and validated with on-call (playbook includes escalation windows, rollback verification steps, and post-incident actions)
No security dependencies block rollout; any customer PII concerns documented and mitigated
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Spec + prototype (2 weeks) — baseline cohorts instrumented in staging. Phase 2: Canary (4 weeks) — enable automated mitigation behind feature flag for <5% traffic on Non-sensitive cohorts. Phase 3: Gradual expansion (6 weeks) — expand to additional cohorts and introduce regulated cohort safeguards (manual approvals). Phase 4: GA (after metrics target met) — feature enabled for all Optimize canaries with opt-out for enterprise customers.
monitoring_signals: Primary accuracy regression (cohort-level delta vs. baseline distribution)
Safety policy violations and adversarial hit-rate increases
Median token latency and p95 tail latency per cohort
Cost per token (inferred) and per-request compute time
Traffic volume and cohort cardinality changes (small cohorts require adjusted thresholds)
alerting_playbook: Green->Amber: auto-notify owners via Slack with suggested actions; no traffic change. Owner must ack within 24h or system escalates.
Amber->Red: automated mitigation applied (traffic cut to 50% or switch to baseline model) and on-call paged immediately. Human review required within 1 hour.
Red persistent (>4h): escalate to Reliability and Product leadership; freeze rollout; prepare incident post-mortem timeline.
False positive suppression: allow transient blips <3 minutes to be ignored unless multiple signals trigger concurrently
dependencies: ENG-20688 (Runtime: traffic shaping APIs and quick-fallback routing)
ENG-20790 (Optimize: signal aggregation pipelines and alerting hooks)
PM-100120 (Customer communication templates for opt-out and SLA notices)
notes: Design tradeoff: balance sensitivity vs. precision; early conservative thresholds preferred for regulated cohorts
Prototype will reuse existing statistical test suite but add cohort-specific baseline windows and sample weighting
Edge case: very small cohorts should use Bayesian shrinkage to avoid overfitting to noise
We should integrate with current rollout A/B tooling to allow progressive traffic splits rather than binary on/off
